findings.title: Orphaned child spans
findings.body:
The default cloud span filter drops successful `errors-only` `PROCESSOR_RUN` spans. The processor docs say these spans exist "so processor-internal work can nest under them." That work (model calls, tool spans, etc.) is still exported, but its `parentSpanId` now points to a span that never reaches the cloud.

Example: a successful errors-only processor makes an LLM call. Its `MODEL_GENERATION` and related child spans upload with a missing parent, which can break the trace tree in the cloud UI.

Consider one of these:
- drop the whole subtree,
- re-parent the children, or
- avoid creating the span and use the fallback context, as `observability: false` does.

findings.title: Breaking default change
findings.body:
The default minimum log level for observability storage changes from `debug` to `warn`, here and in `instances/base.ts`. Existing users who don't set `logging.level` will silently stop getting `debug`/`info` logs in observability storage after upgrading. The PR's own tests had to be updated to opt back into `info`.

The changeset marks this as a `patch` and doesn't mention the change. It should at least be documented in the changeset, and arguably released as a minor version.

findings.title: TripWire no longer error
findings.body:
Legacy-runner TripWire aborts previously ended spans with `processorSpan.error(...)`, which marked them as ERROR in traces. They now end via `end()` with attributes only. Any non-cloud exporter, dashboard, or alert that keys off span error status will no longer see tripwire aborts as errors.

The cloud filter compensates by checking `processorOutcome`; other consumers don't. This changes behavior even for processors that don't opt into `errors-only`.
